why: The candidate draw is mostly noun; every comparable census (007-010) is 100% adjective. Composition alone moves the expected blended rate 1.82% -> ~3.2% with no change in authoring quality, and the comparability rule (reader_model, reader_agent) cannot see it. So the read is stratified, a control arm is authored in the same tick with the same instruments, and the 5% stop condition is applied per stratum - never to the blend. Strata are fixed here, before any fault is seen.

instruments.author: .claude/agents/family-author.md
instruments.rule: unchanged from censuses 007-011; the instrument gate must pass before grading

candidate.selection: Enricher candidates routed by candidate_families.py, cap 20, book-restricted
candidate.comparable_to: census 011 only (noun n=53, verb n=46) - a new baseline for nouns

control.selection: gate-eligible (size>=8, charged>=70%), unauthored, from data/worklist.tsv - the draw censuses 007-010 measured
control.5.3: bastardly pre-skipped (birth-status slur); halal kept with a note; the author reads the draw and may overrule either

stop_condition: any stratum over 5% stops the run for that stratum; the blended rate is reported but decides nothing
read_design: full read of the control arm (~86); candidate arm read at the census sampling rate but never fewer than 50 per stratum where the stratum allows; packets built by census_packets.py; reader sees gloss, charge, note - not which arm

what_a_result_means.control ~1.8%, candidate noun ~3%: pipeline fine; the noun number is a noun number
what_a_result_means.control ~4%+: the tick itself is off - instruments or authoring - not the candidate draw
what_a_result_means.candidate noun >5%, control fine: book-restricted small families hurt authoring; change the cap before authoring more

aggregate_with: census2_aggregate.py --arm candidate=data/families/draft-018.json --arm control=data/families/draft-018-control.json - writes by_arm, by_arm_and_pos and strata_over_threshold; the blended error_rate_pct is still written and still decides nothing. Regression: without --arm the output is identical to census-011-results.json.
scope: every sense authored in stage 9 step 4 that still carries a charge, both arms, drawn complete rather than sampled - as censuses 007-011 were. The 26 senses the collision audit withdrew are not in the population: there is no note left to read.
authoring: 93 parallel family-author agents on Opus 5, family-author.md read verbatim as a registered agent definition, packets written by tools/family_packets.py so the family reached the author as a file rather than a manager's retyping; prompts identical across all 93 and across both arms
pre_read_checks: instrument gate pass (7 instruments unchanged vs HEAD); tone_lint 8 of 543 = 1%, of which 4 are superlative collisions left standing for a decision; sensitive_screen flagged 3 candidate families and 2 control - astounding is a false positive on 'striking dumb with wonder', brother is moot (withdrawn by the collision audit), bastardly stays pre-skipped, halal kept as a dietary-law fact; imbecility ('a stupid mistake') kept - the sense judges an error, not a person

entries.definition: an act intending or showing kindness and good will
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The broadest praise here, naming the good will driving the act as much as the act, whether the kindness lands or is only meant.

entries.definition: a kind act
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and elevated, praising a kind act at a slight remove where *kindness* simply names it.

entries.definition: a considerate and thoughtful act
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Credit for regard paid to someone else — the kindness lies in the care taken, not in warmth as such.

entries.definition: the act of showing affection
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most openly tender of these, since the act is affection displayed rather than care measured out.

entries.definition: an act of gracious kindness
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The kindness comes as something granted graciously, which leaves the receiver holding an obligation *consideration* never creates.

entries.definition: the act of excusing a mistake or offense
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warmer and more inward than *pardon* for the same excusing — a wrong let go rather than officially remitted.

entries.definition: a kind act
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain warm name for the deed itself, with none of the ceremony *benignity* puts around the same act.
examples: whether Mrs. Collins has yet expressed her sense of your kindness in coming to us

entries.definition: a considerate and thoughtful act
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises the noticing behind the deed, where *consideration* praises the regard the deed shows.

entries.definition: an embarrassing mistake
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Heavy and clumsy, a mistake big enough to leave the maker embarrassed by it.

entries.definition: an embarrassing mistake
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and dismissive - the embarrassment is over a job made a mess of, not the single wrong step of *blunder*.

entries.definition: a mistake that results from taking one thing to be another
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the mechanism - one thing taken for another - which lets the mistake sound explicable rather than culpable.
examples: he changed his name in order to avoid confusion with the notorious outlaw

entries.definition: the mistake of misrepresenting the facts
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Named by its result - the facts come out bent - which makes it sound graver than a simple miss like *slip*.

entries.definition: a wrong action attributable to bad judgment or ignorance or inattention
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flattest of these three - the action is simply recorded as wrong, with no reach toward blame.

entries.definition: a stupid mistake
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weightier than *foolishness* - the mistake is named as an act of unwisdom, and the word sounds like a verdict on it.
examples: Selling the land so cheaply was a folly he regretted for years.

entries.definition: a stupid mistake
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest of the stupid-mistake words, chiding where *stupidity* condemns.

entries.definition: a stupid mistake
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The harshest here - a mistake treated as proof of an almost total want of mind.

entries.definition: a mistake resulting from inattention
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Attention gave way for a moment - blameable, but only lightly, and without the clumsiness of *blunder*.

entries.definition: a mistake resulting from neglect
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mistake lies in what went undone, and the neglect in it presses harder than the bare inattention of *oversight*.

entries.definition: a mistake resulting from inattention
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Something went unnoticed, and the word half-excuses the mistake in the act of naming it.

entries.definition: a minor inadvertent mistake usually observed in speech or writing or in small accidents or memory lapses etc.
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The smallest and most forgivable, an unmeant slight miss in speech or writing, a small mishap, a memory that skipped.

entries.definition: an act that brings discredit to the person who does it
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The discrediting act figured as a small mark - smaller, and easier to rub out, than *stain*.

entries.definition: an act that brings discredit to the person who does it
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The discredit sticks - where *spot* can be wiped off, this one is taken to mark the doer.

entries.definition: a stupid mistake
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt: the mistake is named by the mental failing behind it, so the contempt lands on the doer rather than the act.

entries.definition: have the skills and qualifications to do things well
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same compliment pitched cooler than *able* — an appraisal of what someone is equipped to do well rather than a warm word for them.
examples: a capable administrator
children as young as 14 can be extremely capable and dependable
She proved a capable nurse through the long illness.

entries.definition: properly or sufficiently qualified or capable or efficient
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The mildest approval here, since 'properly or sufficiently' sets a threshold and reports it met — qualified, capable or efficient enough, and no claim beyond enough.
examples: a competent typist

entries.definition: able to accomplish a purpose; functioning effectively
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval aimed at the working rather than the worker: the purpose is accomplished and the thing functions, which is a narrower compliment than *able*.
examples: an efficient secretary
the efficient cause of the revolution

entries.definition: worthy of a good workman
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises by holding the thing up to a standard-bearer — worthy of a good workman — which makes it concrete where *competent* stays abstract.
examples: the book is a workmanlike job with chronology and bibliography and index
A workmanlike job

entries.definition: foolish or senseless behavior
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Plain and unbuttoned beside the grander *lunacy*, making the same accusation of madness without the formality.

entries.definition: foolish or senseless behavior
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weighty and censorious - it treats the behaviour as a failure of judgement grave enough to be named, where *craziness* simply calls it mad.
examples: Follies and nonsense, whims and inconsistencies, do divert me, I own, and I laugh at them whenever I can.
to be so honestly blind to the follies and nonsense of others

entries.definition: acting like a clown or buffoon
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Aimed at clowning and buffoonery - antic performance rather than the misjudgement *folly* names, so the disapproval comes with amusement in it.

entries.definition: foolish or senseless behavior
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The softest way of naming senseless behaviour here, framing it as something permitted or allowed oneself rather than something to be condemned.

entries.definition: foolish or senseless behavior
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The hardest word in the set - it does not call the behaviour unwise but insane, and means the charge to land.

entries.definition: the act of moving with great haste
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Great speed as a sudden break away, all abruptness and no blame - the carelessness that shadows *hurry* is absent.

entries.definition: the act of moving with great haste
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Speed as a short spirited burst, brisk and deliberate beside the startled suddenness of *bolt*.
examples: he made a dash for the door

entries.definition: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and weighty, naming the hurry as a fault to be answered for where *hurry* merely reports it.
examples: in his haste to leave he forgot his book
Well, Jane, make haste and tell us; make haste, my love.
In his haste he knocked the cup off the table.

entries.definition: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest name for going fast and going badly at once, with the carelessness carried quietly rather than pressed.
examples: could serve only to amuse her in the hurry and confusion of the following hour

entries.definition: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the weight on momentum - a harder-edged, more headlong version of *hurry*, where the speed is what overrides the care.

entries.definition: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The participle keeps the careless speed running on as an activity rather than a single lapse, unlike the finished act *rush* names.

entries.definition: rushing about hastily in an undignified way
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes the hurry small and skittering, so the loss of dignity comes out as comic rather than damning.

entries.definition: rushing about hastily in an undignified way
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The undignified hurry as graceless floundering - effortful disorder where *scamper* is merely quick and silly.

entries.definition: steadfast in purpose or devotion or affection
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Straightforward praise for not wavering, and it covers purpose, devotion and affection alike rather than loyalty alone.
examples: a man constant in adherence to his ideals
a constant lover
constant as the northern star
She was constant in her affection for him through every trouble.

entries.definition: constant and unchanging
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Absolute and cool: it reports that a thing does not change rather than crediting it with holding fast, so no praise attaches the way it does to *steadfast*.
examples: the immutable laws of nature

entries.definition: firm and dependable especially in loyalty
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Weightier than *constant* because it adds dependability, making the firmness something others can lean on.
examples: a steadfast ally

entries.definition: tireless
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving of what never runs out, measuring steadiness by supply rather than by the refusal to vary that *constant* asks for.
examples: unfailing loyalty
unfailing good spirits

entries.definition: tireless
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same tirelessness as *unfailing*, but figured as a pace that never slackens rather than a store that never empties.
examples: unflagging courtesy

entries.definition: instill (into a person) by constant repetition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and wearing - the thing goes in by sheer relentless repetition, with none of the instruction *inculcate* implies.
examples: he dinned the lessons into his students
His father dinned the same warning into him every single night.

entries.definition: teach and impress by frequent repetitions or admonitions
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and deliberate - repetition put to the work of teaching, and admonition counts as much as drilling.
examples: inculcate values into the young generation

entries.definition: expect, believe, or suppose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The most offhand of these, conceding that the expectation rests on little where *reckon* sounds decided.
examples: I guess she is angry at me for standing her up

entries.definition: expect, believe, or suppose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Reaches the belief by picturing how things must be, so it sounds more speculative than *think* even when it means the same.
examples: I imagine she earned a lot of money with her new novel
the sort of cautiousness to which you, I imagine, have been alluding
don't imagine it was from any silly cause

entries.definition: expect, believe, or suppose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal, and it frames the belief as an opinion delivered rather than a thought privately held as with *think*.

entries.definition: expect, believe, or suppose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal and flatly settled — states the expectation as arrived at, with none of the tentativeness of *suppose*.

entries.definition: expect, believe, or suppose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Holds the belief provisionally, as something granted rather than asserted outright the way *think* asserts it.
examples: "Do you suppose them to be in London?"
There are few people in England, I suppose, who have more true enjoyment of music than myself

entries.definition: hold in suspicion; believe to be guilty
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Belief pointed at a person and against them — where *think* merely holds a view, this one holds someone guilty.
examples: The police suspected him of the theft, but they could prove nothing.

entries.definition: expect, believe, or suppose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain, unmarked way to hold something to be so, without the hedge of *suppose* or the formality of *opine*.
examples: I thought to find her in a bad state
he didn't think to find her in the kitchen
I thought he would arrive before dinner.

entries.definition: not rude; marked by satisfactory (or especially minimal) adherence to social usages and sufficient but not noteworthy consideration for others
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval at its floor: it grants only that the manner was not rude, the minimal end of what *polite* also lets stretch to a satisfactory observance.
examples: even if he didn't like them he should have been civil
Mr. Bingley was unaffectedly civil in his answer, and forced his younger sister to be civil also
It was more than civil; it was really attentive

entries.definition: not rude; marked by satisfactory (or especially minimal) adherence to social usages and sufficient but not noteworthy consideration for others
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Credits the social usages as kept rather than merely the offence as avoided, though the consideration it reports stays sufficient and unremarkable rather than warm.

entries.definition: bewildering or striking dumb with wonder
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The heaviest impact here, and it lands on the person rather than rating the claim - covering both being thrown into confusion and being silenced by wonder.

entries.definition: barely credible
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Leaves the thing just this side of belief where *incredible* puts it past, and the strain it puts on belief sounds like extravagance rather than a fault.
examples: the fabulous endurance of a marathon runner

entries.definition: too improbable to admit of belief
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat measuring word of the set - it sets the odds against the thing and leaves the mockery and the wonder to its neighbours.

entries.definition: beyond belief or understanding
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the thing wholly outside belief or understanding rather than at the far end of the odds, and says nothing about whether what exceeds them is splendid or appalling.
examples: at incredible speed
the book's plot is simply incredible

entries.definition: too improbable to admit of belief
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Refuses belief with wonder still in it: the thing is too wonderful to be admitted, not too flimsy, unlike *tall*.

entries.definition: too improbable to admit of belief
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Dismissive without heat - the claim is treated as stretched in the telling, where *improbable* only weighs the odds.
examples: a tall story
He came home with a tall story about wolves in the lane.

entries.definition: be characteristic of
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flatly descriptive — the trait simply belongs to the thing, and no verdict on its worth comes with it.

entries.definition: be a distinctive feature, attribute, or trait; sometimes in a very positive sense
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The dry one: the trait is what separates this thing from that one, with none of the credit *distinguish* carries.

entries.definition: be a distinctive feature, attribute, or trait; sometimes in a very positive sense
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The member that leans hardest on the very positive reading the sense allows — the trait does not merely identify the thing, it raises it above what stands beside it.

entries.definition: be a distinctive feature, attribute, or trait; sometimes in a very positive sense
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Registers the trait as a sign the thing carries, crediting it lightly where *distinguish* lifts it.
examples: there is that in her features which marks the young woman of distinguished birth
every sentence of her uncle, which marked his intelligence, his taste, or his good manners

entries.definition: accept as true; take to be true
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The unmarked word for taking something to be true, carrying no judgement on whether the acceptance was earned.
examples: We didn't believe his stories from the War
She would not believe the story until she saw the letter herself.

entries.definition: accept as true
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Blunt and informal where *believe* is plain, it treats accepting a claim as taking something on offer, so the acceptance sounds weighed rather than simply held.
examples: I can't buy this story
He says the delay was the weather's fault, but I don't buy that.

entries.definition: believe to be the case
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal, and it frames the belief as arrived at rather than merely held, giving it a footing *believe* does not claim.

entries.definition: believe or accept without questioning or challenge
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Disparaging of the believer rather than the claim, since the gloss builds the absence of questioning into the acceptance itself.
examples: Am I supposed to swallow that story?

entries.definition: believe to be the case
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Softer than *believe*: it presents the belief as settled information one has come by, which lets the speaker hold it lightly.
examples: I understand you have no previous experience?
I understood that there were some very strong objections against the lady.

entries.definition: regard as untrustworthy; regard with suspicion; have no faith or confidence in
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Flat and settled — the plain negative of trusting, delivered as a standing verdict rather than as the charge carried by *suspect*.

entries.definition: regard as untrustworthy; regard with suspicion; have no faith or confidence in
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The wariest of the three, sounding like a misgiving felt about someone rather than a conclusion reached about them.

entries.definition: regard as untrustworthy; regard with suspicion; have no faith or confidence in
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most accusing of these: it does not just withhold faith but pins something on its object, where *distrust* only declines to trust.
examples: I suspect her true motives
She suspected his motives from the first and would not take his help.

entries.definition: morally objectionable behavior
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat, absolute name for conduct that offends morality, condemning without argument or degree.
examples: there is, I believe, in every disposition a tendency to some particular evil, a natural defect

entries.definition: a disrespectful act
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The lightest blame here: an act that withholds due respect rather than one that breaks anything.

entries.definition: a disrespectful act
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Frames the disrespect as a breach, something owed and transgressed, giving the act a hard formal weight that *irreverence* lacks.

entries.definition: morally objectionable behavior
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns the same conduct with a moralizing relish, as though the wrong were knowingly savoured rather than merely done — fuller-blooded than the bare *evil*.

entries.definition: a deliberate pretense or exaggerated display
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Convicts the pretence of being both calculated and laid on too thick, so the fault is excess as much as falsity.

entries.definition: pretending that something is the case in order to make a good impression
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest word here for faking it, faulting the wish to look good rather than the falsehood itself, which is where *pretence* puts the blame.
examples: he is wise enough to assume even the appearance of what is right

entries.definition: the act of giving a false appearance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat, general name for putting up a false front, with none of the flattering motive that softens *appearance* and no charge of overdoing it; British spelling.

entries.definition: pretending that something is the case in order to make a good impression
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Treats the same impression-making pretence as something staged for onlookers, with more of a sneer at the performance than *appearance* carries.
examples: that ceremony is just for show

entries.definition: belligerence aroused by a real or supposed wrong (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain name for the belligerence, and the gloss lets the provoking wrong be merely supposed as readily as real, so the blame lands lighter than in *wrath*.
examples: Anger is counted among the seven deadly sins.

entries.definition: reprehensible acquisitiveness; insatiable desire for wealth (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns while it defines — acquisitiveness called reprehensible and a wanting of wealth that nothing can fill.

entries.definition: spite and resentment at seeing the success of another (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Not simple wanting what another has: the gloss puts spite and resentment at the centre, so the ill-will toward the successful is the sense itself.

entries.definition: reprehensible acquisitiveness; insatiable desire for wealth (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same insatiable greed for wealth as *avarice*, but with a grasping, predatory force in the word rather than a hoarder's.

entries.definition: belligerence aroused by a real or supposed wrong (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same belligerence at real or supposed wrong raised to solemn weight — a word sized for a sin, where *anger* is sized for a mood.

entries.definition: overbearing pride evidenced by a superior manner toward inferiors
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A flat accusation: the swollen self-regard of *pride* has stopped being inward and is now overbearing, worn as a superior manner toward those it counts as inferior.

entries.definition: overbearing pride evidenced by a superior manner toward inferiors
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and chilly, naming the same overbearing pride as a bearing one carries above inferiors rather than levelling the blunt charge *arrogance* makes.

entries.definition: unreasonable and inordinate self-esteem (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Here the word is a vice and not a virtue - self-esteem grown unreasonable and past all proportion, and grave enough to stand as one of the deadly sins.
examples: Everybody is disgusted with his pride.
They had nothing to accuse him of but pride

entries.definition: plead or ask for earnestly
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Asking in a formal key, urged by earnestness rather than by *importune*'s wearing repetition.

entries.definition: call upon in supplication; entreat
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Raises the same entreaty to a pitch of desperation that *beg* states flatly.

entries.definition: beg persistently and urgently
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal, and the persistence lands as a burden on the person asked, where *insist* marks only the asker's refusal to stop.
examples: I importune you to help them

entries.definition: beg persistently and urgently
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Pressing rather than abject - the force sits in refusing to let the asking drop, where *implore* puts it in the emotion behind it.
examples: She insisted and insisted until her father at last agreed to let her go.

entries.definition: call upon in supplication; entreat
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The entreaty in its most formal dress, an appeal made in the posture of supplication rather than *beg*'s bare asking.
examples: Pray forgive me, if I have been very presuming
and pray tell her from me, that she cannot expect to excel, if she does not practise a great deal

entries.definition: ask humbly (for something)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The humility is the whole of it, stated outright and with ceremony, where *beg* leaves the asker's lowness implied.

entries.definition: lure by imitating the characteristic call of an animal
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral and technical here: the enticement is a mimicked animal cry, so the whole of the deception sits in the sound and none of it in any promise.
examples: Call ducks

entries.definition: provoke someone to do something through (often false or exaggerated) promises or persuasion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Works by making the promise attractive rather than by baiting a spot, so the persuasion sounds pleasant even when it is the exaggerated kind.

entries.definition: entice and trap
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The enticing is only half of it — the closing of the trap is the other half, which is what makes this land harder than *entice*.

entries.definition: provoke someone to do something through (often false or exaggerated) promises or persuasion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Draws the person somewhere rather than merely dangling something, and of the three it keeps the falseness of the promise nearest the surface.

entries.definition: provoke someone to do something through (often false or exaggerated) promises or persuasion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The lightest of the three: a promise held out to someone still standing free of it, where *lure* already has them moving.
examples: my friend Denny tempted me further by his account of their present quarters, and the very great attentions

entries.definition: (often followed by ‘with’) full of life and spirit
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Credits life and spirit rather than motion, and leans on a following 'with' to name whatever the thing is brimming over with.
examples: she was wonderfully alive for her age
a face alive with mischief

entries.definition: marked by lively action
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Liveliness as vigorous springing action — sturdier and more robust than *bouncy*, which makes the same spring sound weightless.
examples: a bouncing gait

entries.definition: marked by lively action
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The spring taken as a temperament rather than a feat — lighter and more playful than *bouncing*.
examples: bouncy tunes

entries.definition: fresh and animated
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts freshness beside the animation, so the liveliness comes across as light and easy where *spirited* comes across as strong.
examples: her breezy nature

entries.definition: marked by high spirits or excitement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: High spirits or excitement caught in the act of rising — a thing in motion where *bubbly* names a settled quality.

entries.definition: full of or showing high spirits
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Covers both being full of high spirits and showing them, naming the outward fizz and the inward supply at once.
examples: bright bubbly children
a bubbly personality

entries.definition: uttered with unrestrained enthusiasm
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Moves the fizz into the voice: enthusiasm uttered with nothing holding it back, warm but with an ear on the overflow.

entries.definition: uttered with unrestrained enthusiasm
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Names the quality of that unrestrained enthusiasm rather than a burst of it — looser and more casual than *burbling*.
examples: a novel told in burbly panting tones

entries.definition: marked by high spirits or excitement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The polished word for the same fizz — high spirits or excitement described with a formality the shorter members refuse.
examples: his fertile effervescent mind

entries.definition: marked by high spirits or excitement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The weakest approval of the fizz: the high spirits or excitement are granted, but froth lets them look light and easily dispersed.

entries.definition: full of life and energy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain measure of the family — life and energy stated without a metaphor attached, so every other member here is a way of colouring it.
examples: a lively discussion
lively and attractive parents
a lively party

entries.definition: marked by lively action
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and brisk — lively action as a snap of energy, with none of the dignity *spirited* carries.
examples: the peppy and interesting talk

entries.definition: marked by high spirits or excitement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The brightest of the set — high spirits or excitement that flash and dazzle rather than merely bubble.
examples: scintillating personality

entries.definition: marked by high spirits or excitement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same flash in a smaller, prettier register — decorative where *scintillating* is dazzling.
examples: a row of sparkly cheerleaders

entries.definition: marked by lively action
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The dignified member: lively action with mettle and will behind it, where *peppy* is only pep.
examples: a spirited dance

entries.definition: marked by lively action
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal, and here the lively action is speed — quickness rather than the buoyancy of *bouncy*.

entries.definition: uneducated in the fundamentals of a given art or branch of learning; lacking knowledge of a specific field
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and accusing: the missing fundamentals of one art or branch of learning are laid at the person's door rather than at their schooling's, which is what makes it bite where *untutored* does not.
examples: she is ignorant of quantum mechanics
He is ignorant of chemistry and could not read the label.

entries.definition: uneducated in the fundamentals of a given art or branch of learning; lacking knowledge of a specific field
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Borrows the whole force of being unable to read and drops it on a single field's fundamentals, so a bounded gap in knowledge sounds total — showier scorn than *ignorant*.
examples: he is musically illiterate

entries.definition: lacking knowledge gained by study often in a particular field
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A flat report that knowledge was not gained by study, with or without a particular field in view, and no reproach travels with it — the coolest word here beside *ignorant*.
examples: is unstudied in Latin as he is in may other matters

entries.definition: lacking in schooling
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mild and almost exculpating, since it puts the deficiency in the schooling that was never had rather than in the head that went without it.
examples: an untutored genius

entries.definition: act as an informer
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Casts the act as a role rather than an occasion — you are not someone who spoke but an informer, and the faint taint sits in that role where *tell* has none.
examples: He informed on his own brother to the police.

entries.definition: give evidence
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest verb available for producing evidence, naming the act and implying nothing about the one who does it.

entries.definition: to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Says only that something has been swelled; the fault lies in the going beyond, not in the verb, which is why it accuses least of the three.

entries.definition: cause someone to believe an untruth
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same planting of a false belief, but the word frames it as a breach of the trust that made the believing possible, which is what makes it the heaviest term here.

entries.definition: cause someone to believe an untruth
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the act by its result — the untruth has landed and is believed — where *mislead* stops at the information handed over.
examples: I never meant to deceive you, but my spirits might often lead me wrong.
Caroline is incapable of wilfully deceiving anyone

entries.definition: to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain charge of overstatement, taking in both going past reasonable bounds and going past the truth, and always implying the real measure is smaller.
examples: tended to romanticize and exaggerate this ‘gracious Old South’ imagery

entries.definition: tell an untruth; pretend with intent to deceive
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Flat and unsoftened, covering both the untruth spoken and the pretence behind it, with no room left for an innocent reading.
examples: Don't lie to your parents

entries.definition: to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes the thing itself loom larger, so the overreach shows in the size of the picture rather than in a claim stated outright.

entries.definition: give false or misleading information to
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest of the deceptions: it charges only the false or misleading information given and leaves intent unsettled, where *lie* settles it.

entries.definition: of the most contemptible kind
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and absolute, it puts the thing at the very floor of the scale with none of *low-down*'s sneer.
examples: abject cowardice

entries.definition: deserving of contempt or scorn
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The family's plain verdict: it states that scorn is deserved without supplying any of the scorn itself, where *scummy* supplies nothing else.

entries.definition: of the most contemptible kind
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal, and the trailing particle adds a drawled contempt that flat *low* leaves out.
examples: a low-down sneak

entries.definition: of the most contemptible kind
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: One blunt syllable for the bottom of the scale, carrying the direction of the fall and nothing more.
examples: a low stunt to pull
a low-down sneak

entries.definition: of no value or worth
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Writes a thing off as amounting to nothing, a dismissal by worthlessness rather than the earned scorn of *contemptible*.

entries.definition: of the most contemptible kind
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contempt with wretchedness folded into it, so the thing comes off squalid as well as low.
examples: his miserable treatment of his family
You miserable skunk!

entries.definition: inspiring mixed contempt and pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contempt leads and pity trails: the scorn is the louder half of the mixture.
examples: their efforts were pathetic

entries.definition: inspiring mixed contempt and pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentler face of the same mixed response, letting the pity carry the weight the contempt in *pathetic* takes.
examples: pitiable lack of character

entries.definition: inspiring mixed contempt and pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Holds both halves at once, asking you to feel sorry for the thing and look down on it in the same breath.
examples: pitiful exhibition of cowardice

entries.definition: of the most contemptible kind
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most physically disgusted of these, treating the utterly contemptible as filth you would rather not touch.
examples: a scummy rabble

entries.definition: of the most contemptible kind
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Comes out as a curse rather than an assessment, the contempt thrown instead of delivered.
examples: a scurvy trick

entries.definition: indicate by marking trees with blazes
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Literal where *mark* is figurative: the sign is cut into trees, so the word carries its instrument and nothing evaluative.
examples: blaze a trail

entries.definition: mark with a buoy
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The whole force of the word sits in the marker it names, so it points a thing out without commenting on it.

entries.definition: indicate the dimensions on
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Technical and flatly informative — what it puts on a thing is measurements, with none of the singling-out for notice that *distinguish* carries.
examples: These techniques permit us to dimension the human heart

entries.definition: make conspicuous or noteworthy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The only member that raises its object rather than merely labelling it, conferring either conspicuousness or the status of being worth remark, where *mark* just designates.
examples: Mr. Bingley had danced with her twice, and she had been distinguished by his sisters.
with no further attempt to distinguish Elizabeth

entries.definition: designate as if by a mark
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain designating verb, working by figure as readily as by an actual mark and passing no judgement on what it singles out.

entries.definition: reveal unintentionally
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The teller never meant to tell: the thing escapes and gives the person away, so the fault is in the letting slip rather than the intent.

entries.definition: divulge confidential information or secrets
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Dismissive — the confidence falls out of an ungoverned mouth for no motive beyond the pleasure of talking.

entries.definition: cause to be revealed and jeopardized
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The revealing wrecks what it reveals — where *disclose* only makes a thing known, this one endangers it in the same motion.
examples: The story blew their cover
The double agent was blown by the other side

entries.definition: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the hidden thing into public circulation all at once, with the abruptness of the arrival rather than any blame as its whole character.
examples: he broke the news to her
With the kindest concern he came on to Longbourn, and broke his apprehensions to us in a manner most creditable to his heart.

entries.definition: reveal in private; tell confidentially
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The one telling here that keeps the secret a secret: it goes to a single hearer in trust, where *divulge* gives it away.

entries.definition: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and procedural: it makes the matter public without the flavour of trust broken that *divulge* carries.
examples: The auction house would not disclose the price at which the van Gogh had sold

entries.definition: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Here the act is the telling, not the finding: flat about how the thing got out and saying only that it is now public.

entries.definition: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Keeps the secrecy in view — what is told was meant to be kept, so the telling registers as a breach.

entries.definition: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Strips the cover off with the implication that the thing was kept back for a reason, so the telling lands as a charge against whoever kept it.
examples: Till I can forget his father, I can never defy or expose him.
Surely there can be no occasion for exposing him so dreadfully.

entries.definition: tell anonymously
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: What the word specifies is the missing name — the telling happens with the teller kept out of sight, and it passes no verdict on what is told.

entries.definition: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The neutral centre the others specialise — something hidden is made visible, with no comment on who loses by it.
examples: The actress won't reveal how old she is

entries.definition: divulge confidential information or secrets
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contemptuous: the secret is handed over the way an informer hands it over, and the handing over is the disgrace.

entries.definition: produce or disclose suddenly or unexpectedly
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: All timing and no secrecy — whether the thing is produced or disclosed, the force of the word is that it arrives with no warning.
examples: He sprang the news on me just as I was leaving

entries.definition: divulge confidential information or secrets
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The bare verb for someone entrusted failing to stay quiet; it names no content, only that the confidence got out of them.

entries.definition: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Treats the matter as buried rather than merely untold, so the digging is part of the word in a way it is not in *reveal*.

entries.definition: the act of preventing
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and absolute: where *interference* only slows or hampers, this names prevention accomplished, with no hint of how it was done.
examples: there was no bar against leaving

entries.definition: the act of hindering or obstructing or impeding
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The broadest of the three, covering hindering, obstructing and impeding alike, and it frames the act as a course disrupted from outside rather than a way simply blocked.
examples: She looked at her father to entreat his interference, lest Mary should be singing all night.
never had she before been so much disposed to pardon his interference in the views of his friend

entries.definition: the act of obstructing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts something in the way, so the check is felt as a mass to be got around rather than *bar*'s clean stop.
examples: obstruction of justice

entries.definition: yield (to); give satisfaction to
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The satisfaction is handed over outright and the pleasure of it is the whole point, where *indulge* reaches the same result by giving way.
examples: had been gratifying his vanity by encouraging the preference which she believed she had most incautiously shown

entries.definition: put into a good mood
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: American spelling of the same move, and it measures success by the mood produced, not by any demand met.

entries.definition: put into a good mood
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: British spelling; the target is the person's mood rather than their want, so it works on temper where *gratify* works on desire.

entries.definition: yield (to); give satisfaction to
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Keeps the yielding in view, so the satisfaction reads as a resistance dropped rather than a gift made.

entries.definition: giving spirit and vivacity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm approval aimed at spirit rather than muscle - what it gives is vivacity, not the strength *invigorating* claims.

entries.definition: imparting vitality and energy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval with a bite in it - the energy arrives sharply, where *refreshing* delivers the same energy gently.
examples: the bracing mountain air

entries.definition: imparting vitality and energy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Mild and matter-of-fact praise that renders vitality as pace and snap rather than as depth of force.

entries.definition: giving spirit and vivacity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same gift of spirit as *animating*, but framed as a lift applied to something that was flat before.

entries.definition: making lively and cheerful
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The high end of the family - the lift goes past energy into open cheerfulness, which *stimulating* stops short of.
examples: the exhilarating effect of mountain air

entries.definition: imparting vitality and energy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The simplest word in the group for this energy, crediting clarity and cleanness with the lift that *bracing* wins by sharpness.

entries.definition: imparting strength and vitality
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain, full-strength word for the effect, and the only one here that promises strength as well as liveliness, where *enlivening* offers spirit alone.
examples: the invigorating mountain air

entries.definition: giving or having the power to give life and spirit
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most absolute claim available here, since what it grants is life and spirit outright rather than a boost to either.
examples: returning the life-giving humus to the land
life-giving love and praise

entries.definition: imparting vitality and energy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Identical in force to *refreshing* but stiffer in build, which lends the same lift a formal weight.

entries.definition: imparting vitality and energy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Easy, grateful approval - the energy it names reads as relief from tiredness rather than as a charge of power.

entries.definition: tending to impart new life and vigor to
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval for a lift that is a return of something lost - new life and vigor given back, not given for the first time as in *life-giving*.
examples: the renewing warmth of the sunshine

entries.definition: tending to impart new life and vigor to
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Names the same power of return as a settled property of the thing, calmer and more formal than the active *renewing*.

entries.definition: making lively and cheerful
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cooler than *exhilarating* for the same effect, naming the rousing of liveliness and good cheer without saying how high it rises.

entries.definition: imparting vitality and energy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cool, measured approval that credits a thing with steadying and energizing rather than delighting, unlike the showier *exhilarating*.

entries.definition: giving or having the power to give life and spirit
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same gift of life and spirit as *life-giving*, stated as a working effect rather than as the grand attribute.
examples: the vitalizing rays of the warming sun

entries.definition: lovable especially in a childlike or naive way
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Superlative where *lovable* is merely descriptive - affection is not attracted but compelled, and the childlike or naive streak is what compels it.

entries.definition: having a sweet nature befitting an angel or cherub
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Lifts sweetness to an ideal - praise that leaves no room for a fault in the nature described.
examples: an angelic smile

entries.definition: having a sweet nature befitting an angel or cherub
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The extended form of *angelic*, reaching for the same unblemished sweetness with a more formal ring.

entries.definition: having a sweet nature befitting an angel or cherub
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Takes the cherub rather than the angel: sweetness that is small, round and fond instead of exalted.
examples: a cherubic face

entries.definition: inviting cuddling or hugging
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Carries the invitation in its build - a thing that asks to be held, stated more deliberately than *cuddly*.
examples: a cuddlesome baby

entries.definition: inviting cuddling or hugging
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Soft, offhand and physical: the appeal is being huggable, not being good-natured as in *sweet*.
examples: a cuddly teddybear

entries.definition: lovable especially in a childlike or naive way
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts the effect in motion rather than the quality at rest: it wins affection over, where *adorable* simply announces the winning is done.

entries.definition: having characteristics that attract love or affection
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The family's plain baseline - it says the thing has whatever draws love, without dressing the quality up as innocence or sweetness.
examples: a mischievous but lovable child

entries.definition: having characteristics that attract love or affection
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The full-spelt form, identical in warmth and force to *lovable*.

entries.definition: lovable especially in a childlike or naive way
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Broad, easy warmth for the same childlike appeal, without the surrender *adorable* implies.

entries.definition: having a sweet nature befitting an angel or cherub
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most rarefied of the angel words - sweetness raised to something radiant and remote, well past the homely warmth of *cherubic*.
examples: looking so seraphic when he slept

entries.definition: having a sweet nature befitting an angel or cherub
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The unadorned name for the nature the angel words put wings on - the same quality with none of the exaltation.
examples: a sweet disposition

entries.definition: beyond normal limits
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat statement of the case, that the limit has been passed, without the indignation *unreasonable* adds to it.
examples: excessive charges

entries.definition: far more than usual or expected
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The one member whose excess can flatter, registering a degree far past what was expected as remarkable rather than as a fault.
examples: an extraordinary desire for approval
Elizabeth was chiefly struck with his extraordinary deference for Lady Catherine

entries.definition: far beyond a norm in quantity or amount or degree; to an utmost degree
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names the utmost degree flatly, measuring how far a quantity, amount or degree sits from the norm without ruling on whether that is a fault.
examples: an extreme example
extreme temperatures
extreme danger

entries.definition: beyond a norm in opinion or actions
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely positional: it sets an opinion or action out past the norm and leaves the verdict to whoever is looking, where *outrageous* is all verdict.
examples: the far right

entries.definition: beyond normal limits
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and cool, sizing the overshoot rather than complaining about it as *unreasonable* does.
examples: a book of inordinate length

entries.definition: greatly exceeding bounds of reason or moderation
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The hottest word here: the excess is treated as an affront, and the word demands that someone object.
examples: spends an outrageous amount on entertainment

entries.definition: (used of opinions and actions) far beyond the norm
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Marks opinions and actions as standing well past the norm by commitment rather than by accident of degree, and eyes that commitment with reserve.
examples: radical opinions on education

entries.definition: far more than usual or expected
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sizes an excess by calling it a wrong, so the same far-more-than-expected that *extraordinary* admires becomes something to answer for.

entries.definition: complete or extreme
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Absolute rather than excessive, saying a thing is complete or extreme with nothing softening it, so its force is bleakness rather than blame.
examples: stark poverty
a stark contrast

entries.definition: greatly exceeding bounds of reason or moderation
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and dry, registering a large overshoot as a grumble rather than the protest that *outrageous* makes of the same gloss.

entries.definition: (used of opinions and actions) far beyond the norm
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A bare intensifier of position that shoves an opinion or action to the far edge and says nothing about it beyond how far out it sits.
examples: an ultra conservative

entries.definition: beyond normal limits
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the excess for not being warranted rather than for its bulk, the quietest complaint among the words sharing its gloss.
examples: his dress stops just short of undue elegance

entries.definition: beyond normal limits
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Convicts the overstepping of having no argument for itself, a heavier charge than the plain over-the-limit of *excessive*.
examples: unreasonable demands

entries.definition: befitting or characteristic of a young boy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Mildly fond, measuring against a young boy whether the thing suits one or simply resembles one.
examples: a boyish grin

entries.definition: very young
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral and intensifying, pushing youth to its very beginning and saying how far along rather than how it looks.
examples: at an early age

entries.definition: including or intended for youthful persons
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely classificatory, sorting by who is taken in or aimed at, with none of the approval in *youthful*.
examples: a junior sports league
junior fashions

entries.definition: (of children and animals) young, immature
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warmth sits in the diminutive: the child or young animal is made endearing, where *small* only measures.
examples: what a big little boy you are
Her little brother was not yet old enough for school.

entries.definition: (of children and animals) young, immature
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Plain and unsentimental about the same young creature as *little*, sized rather than cherished.
examples: small children

entries.definition: young and immature
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Youth felt as softness, the immaturity something breakable rather than something admired.
examples: at a tender age

entries.definition: suggestive of youth; vigorous and fresh
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Literary and elevated where *young* and *youthful* are plain, admiring the vigour rather than merely reporting it.

entries.definition: suggestive of youth; vigorous and fresh
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm and direct, counting no years at all but the vigour and freshness that read as youth, and asserting it flatly where *youngish* hedges.
examples: he is young for his age
At sixty her step was still young.

entries.definition: somewhat young
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Hedged and faintly grudging, granting youth only approximately where *young* grants it outright.

entries.definition: suggestive of youth; vigorous and fresh
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts youth forward as a resemblance rather than a fact, so the freshness carries the whole of the claim.

entries.definition: disappoint, prove undependable to; abandon, forsake
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same desertion as *fail*, but framed as trust broken against the person left behind, which is why it is the heaviest word here.

entries.definition: fail to meet the hopes or expectations of
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest of the three: hopes or expectations simply come up short, with none of *fail*'s claim that someone was depended on and abandoned.
examples: Here are officers enough at Meryton to disappoint all the young ladies in the country.
Miss Bingley, however, was incapable of disappointing Mr. Darcy in anything

entries.definition: disappoint, prove undependable to; abandon, forsake
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the weight on not being there when relied on, covering both the proving undependable and the walking away, but stated as a lapse rather than a wrong.
examples: Elizabeth's courage did not fail her.

entries.definition: lacking in power or forcefulness
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Turns the same want of power into a judgement — force was expected here and it is not there.
examples: an ineffectual ruler

entries.definition: lacking in power or forcefulness
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the missing power or forcefulness as a plain attribute, without the verdict *ineffectual* passes on it.
examples: like an unable phoenix in hot ashes
His unable protests did nothing to stop the sale.

entries.definition: marked by depth of thinking
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain, unshowy praise that locates the depth in the thinking itself rather than in the person's habit of it, as *thoughtful* does.
examples: deep thoughts
a deep allegory
For you are a young lady of deep reflection, I know, and read great books

entries.definition: showing intellectual penetration or emotional depth
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The strongest of these and the widest, crediting either a mind that cuts through or a feeling that runs deep, where *deep* and *thoughtful* stay with the intellect.
examples: the differences are profound
a profound insight
a profound book
a profound mind
profound contempt
profound regret

entries.definition: having intellectual depth
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Mild, steady approval for possessing intellectual depth, without the reach *profound* claims.
examples: a deeply thoughtful essay

entries.definition: according with custom or propriety
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm approval - what accords with custom is credited with grace rather than mere compliance, unlike the dry *decorous*.
examples: her becoming modesty

entries.definition: according with custom or propriety
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Gentle and pleased - it finds conduct agreeable in its accord with propriety rather than measuring it against a rule.
examples: comely behavior

entries.definition: according with custom or propriety
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A phrase rather than a word, and formal to the point of ceremony - approval delivered by invoking the code instead of describing the conduct.
examples: it is not comme il faut for a gentleman to be constantly asking for money

entries.definition: socially right or correct
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval as a verdict - the social rule was met, and nothing warmer than that is claimed.
examples: correct behavior

entries.definition: in harmony with the spirit of particular persons or occasion
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Modest and human - it grants that a thing suits the persons and the moment, with less deliberation than *fitting*.
examples: a decent burial

entries.definition: according with custom or propriety
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cool and external - conduct is held up against a standard of propriety and passes, with none of the warmth of *becoming*.

entries.definition: in harmony with the spirit of particular persons or occasion
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approval keyed to the occasion and the people in it rather than to any code - it praises harmony where *correct* praises compliance.
examples: we have come to dedicate a portion of that field … It is altogether fitting and proper that we should do this

entries.definition: proper or legitimate according to Muslim law
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A designation rather than a compliment - it states that something is proper or legitimate under a named law, and the approval belongs to that law and not to the speaker.
examples: the fund earns halal profits in full compliance with the Shari'a

entries.definition: proper or legitimate
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and reassuring - declares a thing proper or legitimate, above board and open to no objection.

entries.definition: exaggeratedly proper
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contemptuous - the excess of propriety is read as self-satisfaction, correctness worn as superiority over others.

entries.definition: exaggeratedly proper
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The lightest fault in this group - propriety held so tightly it stiffens, mocked rather than condemned.

entries.definition: exaggeratedly proper
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Dismissive and faintly ridiculing - the overdone propriety is treated as fussiness, silly rather than severe like *priggish*.

entries.definition: exaggeratedly proper
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Propriety inflated into squeamishness - more disapproving than *prim*, since the excess is taken as a readiness to be shocked.

entries.definition: socially right or correct
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The bluntest way to render the same social judgement as *correct*, carrying no formality at all.
examples: it isn't right to leave the party without saying goodbye

entries.definition: according with custom or propriety
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Understated - grants that conduct accords with propriety without the ceremony *decorous* brings to the same verdict.
examples: seemly behavior

entries.definition: fixed in your purpose
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: States only that the purpose is fixed and passes no verdict on it, where *steadfast* and *stalwart* praise.
examples: bent on going to the theater

entries.definition: desperately determined
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Determination pushed to its extreme edge, where the resolve looks driven rather than chosen.

entries.definition: characterized by great determination
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Says the will outright and says there is a lot of it, with none of the hardness metaphor carried by *firm* or *stiff*.
examples: a struggle against a determined enemy

entries.definition: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Resolution felt as something pressed against and not giving - resistance where *steady* offers only constancy.
examples: firm convictions
a firm mouth

entries.definition: firm in purpose or belief; characterized by firmness and determination
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and settled, and it covers belief as well as purpose - firmness treated as a standing quality of the person, not a stand taken once.
examples: stood resolute against the enemy
faced with a resolute opposition
a resolute and unshakeable faith

entries.definition: dependable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Dependability raised to staunchness - stronger praise than *stout*, and it suggests standing by as well as standing up.
examples: the stalwart citizens at Lexington
a stalwart supporter of the UN

entries.definition: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The warmest of the unshakable four - firmness praised as something held faithfully over time.
examples: steadfast resolve

entries.definition: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The evenest word here - determination as a level that never dips, without the hardness *firm* and *stiff* put into it.
examples: Steady to his purpose, he scarcely spoke ten words to her through the whole of Saturday

entries.definition: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Unshakable, but by rigidity - the resolve reads as unbending as much as strong.

entries.definition: dependable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Hearty approval - dependable in the way something sturdy is, solid enough to take weight.
examples: stout hearts

entries.definition: unshaken in purpose
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The purpose holds against something that might have cowed it - it implies the attempt was made and failed.

entries.definition: unshaken in purpose
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The flat negative of the same idea - the purpose simply did not move, without the note of fear faced down in *undaunted*.

entries.definition: make illegal payments to in exchange for favors or influence
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the payment as the offence it is, an accusation rather than the sardonic understatement of *buy*.

entries.definition: make illegal payments to in exchange for favors or influence
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word for a purchase turned on a person, so the contempt lies in the implication - they had a price - where *bribe* states the illegality outright.
examples: This judge can be bought
They said the inspector had been bought and would report whatever he was told.

entries.definition: having the nature of vice
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the thing as vice itself rather than describing a fault in it, which makes it absolute where *wicked* is merely damning.

entries.definition: extremely wicked, deeply criminal
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and heavy-syllabled, delivering the same extreme-and-criminal verdict as *heinous* in a more elevated register.
examples: a flagitious crime

entries.definition: (of an actor or role) being or playing the villain
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A casting word: it marks the villain's part, or the actor filling it, and condemns nobody.
examples: Iago is the heavy role in ‘Othello’

entries.definition: extremely wicked, deeply criminal
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The blunt public condemnation, wickedness pitched so far into the criminal that the word works almost as a sentence.
examples: heinous accusations

entries.definition: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gravest of its group, weighing the wrong as an enormity rather than simply logging it as sin like *sinful*.
examples: iniquitous deeds

entries.definition: insusceptible of reform
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pictures reform as recovery and denies it — nothing here can be got back.
examples: vicious irreclaimable boys

entries.definition: insusceptible of reform
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest of these four, since redemption is what it withholds: a final verdict rather than a prognosis.
examples: irredeemable sinners

entries.definition: extremely wicked
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns the wickedness in the abstract, where *villainous* points instead at the one committing it.
examples: nefarious schemes

entries.definition: liable to sin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest here by a wide margin: it concedes only that sin is possible, not that any has been done.
examples: a frail and peccable mortal

entries.definition: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest naming of wickedness-as-sin, condemnatory without the swell of *iniquitous*.
examples: he said it was sinful to wear lipstick

entries.definition: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Measures the wickedness as distance from godliness, so the fault is a standing away rather than *sinful*'s committed offence.
examples: ungodly acts

entries.definition: insusceptible of reform
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same refusal built on a blunt negative prefix, more workaday in sound than *irredeemable*.

entries.definition: insusceptible of reform
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flattest of the group, stating only that reform will not take, with none of *irredeemable*'s note of lost salvation.

entries.definition: having the nature of vice
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Presents vice as the settled bent of the thing, so it sounds like a diagnosis of character beside *evil*'s flat sentence.

entries.definition: extremely wicked
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Casts the extreme wickedness as a villain's, making it a fact of character rather than of the deed.
examples: a villainous plot
a villainous band of thieves

entries.definition: morally bad in principle or practice
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain, unhedged moral verdict, and it covers both the settled principle and the actual practice rather than choosing between them.

entries.definition: deprive somebody of something by deceit
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The hardest word here: the lie has a victim who is out something, and the loss is built into the charge.

entries.definition: deprive somebody of something by deceit
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal, and the pettiness is the sting — the same deceitful taking as *cheat*, cut down to something small and mean.

entries.definition: be false to; be dishonest with
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain, flat accusation of bad faith — it names the dishonesty and stops there, without saying what anyone got out of it.
examples: He deceived the friend who had trusted him most.

entries.definition: be false to; be dishonest with
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Heavier than *deceive* because the falseness is aimed at the other person's mind, leaving them settled in something untrue.

entries.definition: the trait of lacking enthusiasm for or interest in things generally
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest word here for the same trait: caring about nothing, weighed as a fault rather than merely reported.

entries.definition: the trait of lacking enthusiasm for or interest in things generally
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the want of enthusiasm or interest as a settled disposition, stating it without the reproach *apathy* attaches to the same trait.
examples: Years of illness had left him in a settled indifference to everything around him.

entries.definition: inactivity resulting from lethargy and lack of vigor or energy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Traces the inactivity to lethargy and drained energy, so it reads as something suffered rather than a withholding.

entries.definition: the trait of lacking enthusiasm for or interest in things generally
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Casts the missing interest as feeling gone dull rather than a stance taken, which blunts the blame *apathy* carries.

entries.definition: the trait of remaining inactive; a lack of initiative
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flattest member: staying inactive and starting nothing, with no claim about what is or isn't felt underneath.

entries.definition: good-natured tolerance of delay or incompetence
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal, and it makes the same tolerance sound deliberately held back - a reaction withheld where *patience* is simply an even temper.

entries.definition: a disposition to kindness and compassion
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The warmest of the three and the widest: not endurance of an annoyance but a whole bent toward kindness and compassion.
examples: the victor's grace in treating the vanquished

entries.definition: good-natured tolerance of delay or incompetence
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain praise for a temper that absorbs delay or bungling without souring, the trait named as if it cost nothing.
examples: I recollected my dear Elizabeth and Jane, and for their sakes had patience with her.
She tried, however, to compose herself to answer him with patience

entries.definition: harshness of manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal, and it locates the fault in bearing and manner rather than in feeling, which makes the condemnation cool and considered.

entries.definition: a dislike of anything that causes delay
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The narrowest fault here - it fastens on one trigger, delay, and so criticises without alleging the loss of control that *temper* does.
examples: His impatience showed in every queue he ever stood in.

entries.definition: harshness of manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word for the same harsh manner, felt as a cutting edge on how someone deals with you rather than *asperity*'s formal verdict on them.

entries.definition: a disposition to exhibit uncontrolled anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest charge in the family: not a passing mood but a settled liability to anger that gets out of hand, so attributing it is an accusation about character.
examples: his temper was well known to all his employees
He has a temper, and everyone at work knows to keep out of his way.

entries.definition: secrecy
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal and clipped where *secrecy* is abstract, shrinking the same trait to one syllable of keeping quiet.
examples: mum's the word

entries.definition: the trait of keeping things secret
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat name for the trait, taking no view on whether what is kept back ought to be.
examples: Having said thus much, I feel no doubt of your secrecy.
There were few people on whose secrecy she would have more confidently depended

entries.definition: the trait of keeping things secret
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names the trait by its outward result — nothing said — where *secrecy* names the keeping back itself.

entries.definition: the trait of remaining calm and seeming not to care; a casual lack of concern
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Leans on the not-caring half of the sense rather than the calm half, so the composure reads as something missing and carries a faint reproach that *unconcern* escapes.
examples: He listened to her with perfect indifference
With an air of indifference, he soon afterwards added

entries.definition: the trait of remaining calm and seeming not to care; a casual lack of concern
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Weights the calm, casual side instead — an untroubled evenness that may be only a seeming, and names the absent worry without *indifference*'s hint that nothing is felt at all.

entries.definition: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A respectable-looking surface lent to something so it seems defensible; it does not hide the thing underneath, it only shades it.
examples: the situation soon took on a different color

entries.definition: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British spelling of the same deceptive surface: a creditable tint lent to something so it passes, and no more than a tint, where *disguise* covers.
examples: His story was only a colour to hide what he had really done.

entries.definition: an outward semblance that misrepresents the true nature of something
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most covering word here, not a shading of the truth but an outward form that actively misrepresents what lies under it.
examples: the theatrical notion of disguise is always associated with catastrophe in his stories

entries.definition: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
entries.label: negative
