entries.tone: Carries the idea of a polish worked onto the outside, so the deceit is one of finish rather than of concealment as in *disguise*.
examples: he tried to give his falsehood the gloss of moral sanction

entries.definition: an artful or simulated semblance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same artful or simulated semblance as *pretence*, but framed as a form put on and worn, so the deceit sits in the assuming of it.
examples: under the guise of friendship he betrayed them

entries.definition: an artful or simulated semblance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British spelling, and it foregrounds the artfulness, naming the semblance as something got up rather than something merely appearing.

entries.definition: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The barest word in the set, naming only the outward or token form and leaving the misleading to be inferred, where *pretence* puts the artifice on show.
examples: he hoped his claims would have a semblance of authenticity

entries.definition: a blemish on the skin that is formed before birth
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Traces the blemish to birth rather than to any injury, so nothing is blamed for it.

entries.definition: a mark or flaw that spoils the appearance of something (especially on a person's body)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Keeps the damage at the level of appearance — the thing is spoiled to look at, where *defect* calls it faulty.
examples: a facial blemish

entries.definition: a place or area that has been burned (especially on a person's body)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the place by the violence that made it, which gives it a weight *mark* has not.

entries.definition: a mark left after a small piece has been chopped or broken off of something
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The colourless name for the same loss *chip* reports, with none of the sound of breaking in it.

entries.definition: a mark left after a small piece has been chopped or broken off of something
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Something is gone rather than merely marked, and the word makes the loss sound abrupt.

entries.definition: a blemish resulting from a break without complete separation of the parts
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Graver than *chip* or *scratch*, since the break runs through the thing and only the parts still holding together keep it whole.
examples: there was a crack in the mirror

entries.definition: a mark or flaw that spoils the appearance of something (especially on a person's body)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the spoiling mark as a fault, so the thing carrying it is judged wanting rather than merely marked.
examples: A faint scar was the only defect on her smooth skin.

entries.definition: an impression in a surface (as made by a blow)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The surface has given way under a blow without breaking, so nothing is lost and it stays milder than *chip*.

entries.definition: an impression in a surface (as made by a blow)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and belittling — the same blow-struck impression as *dent*, named in a way that makes light of it.

entries.definition: an indication of damage
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flattest word here: it registers that damage happened and passes no verdict, where *scar* insists the damage lasted.

entries.definition: a small congenital pigmented spot on the skin
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely descriptive: a pigmented spot carried from birth, with no suggestion of damage or fault.

entries.definition: an impression in a surface (as made by a blow)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Smallest of the impressions, and the word makes the blow sound trifling where *dent* concedes real force.

entries.definition: an indication of damage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest of the damage words: the harm is over but permanently recorded, where *scratch* passes.

entries.definition: an indication of damage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Damage dragged across a surface — broader than *scratch* and still shallow.

entries.definition: an indication of damage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The slightest indication of damage in the set — thin and superficial where *scar* is permanent.

entries.definition: a skin lesion that is a diagnostic sign of some disease
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Clinical and grave: the lesion is not merely present but read as evidence, the skin testifying to a disease.

entries.definition: (pathology) a firm abnormal elevated blemish on the skin; caused by a virus
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Clinical naming for a raised growth, but abnormality is built into it — not the plain report *mole* makes.

entries.definition: elegance by virtue of fineness of manner and expression
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Places the elegance in fineness of manner and expression, praising a person's polish rather than any effect they make.

entries.definition: the quality of being magnificent or splendid or grand
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Magnificence that dazzles, adding glitter where *grandeur* adds height.
examples: his ‘Hamlet’ lacks the brilliance that one expects

entries.definition: elegance in dress or behavior
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and flatly approving: elegance of dress or behaviour named in one blunt syllable.
examples: she has a lot of class

entries.definition: the quality of being beautiful and delicate in appearance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The homelier name for beauty in fineness, prettier and less lofty in sound than *delicacy*.
examples: the daintiness of her touch

entries.definition: distinctive and stylish elegance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same stylish elegance with spirit in it, brisk and showy where *style* is merely distinctive.
examples: he wooed her with the confident dash of a cavalry officer

entries.definition: the quality of being beautiful and delicate in appearance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises beauty that is fine rather than bold, the softest note in a family that runs to *grandeur*.
examples: The delicacy of the lace made it look like frost on a window.

entries.definition: ceremonial elegance and splendor
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Ceremonial splendour with a flourish on it — the dazzle the occasion throws off, where *pomp* is the display itself.
examples: entered with much eclat in a coach drawn by eight white horses

entries.definition: a refined quality of gracefulness and good taste
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain central name for the quality — gracefulness and good taste, with no dazzle asked of it.
examples: she conveys an aura of elegance and gentility
Lady Catherine is far from requiring that elegance of dress in us which becomes herself and daughter.
I never saw such capacity, and taste, and application, and elegance, as you describe, united.

entries.definition: the quality of being magnificent or splendid or grand
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Elevated and imposing — splendour on a scale that asks to be looked up at.
examples: an imaginative mix of old-fashioned grandeur and colorful art

entries.definition: the quality of being magnificent or splendid or grand
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The largest word here — grandeur and splendour taken together at full strength, with nothing held back.
examples: for magnificence and personal service there is the Queen's hotel

entries.definition: ceremonial elegance and splendor
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Binds the splendour to ceremony, so the praise falls on the staging rather than on the thing staged.

entries.definition: elegance by virtue of being fashionable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Measures the elegance by fashion, approving of being current in a way *elegance* never is.

entries.definition: the quality of being magnificent or splendid or grand
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Full-throated praise for the magnificent, glowing where *grandeur* towers.
examples: it is the university that gives the scene its stately splendor

entries.definition: the quality of being magnificent or splendid or grand
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The British spelling of *splendor*, identical to it in force.

entries.definition: distinctive and stylish elegance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving and self-assured: elegance with a signature on it, where *elegance* alone can be impersonal.
examples: she had no conversation, no style, no taste, no beauty

entries.definition: the humane quality of understanding the suffering of others and wanting to do something about it
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The warmest word in the set: understanding that already carries the will to do something, not merely to be moved.
examples: She was proud that in a cause of compassion and honour he had been able to get the better of himself.

entries.definition: tendency to be kind and forgiving
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plainest word for the disposition, warm and unceremonious where *mercy* makes the same forgivingness sound grave.
examples: Her kindness was such that she never held anything against him for long.

entries.definition: a disposition to be kind and forgiving
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Grave and elevated where *kindness* is homely, giving the same forgiving disposition the weight of a virtue.

entries.definition: mercifulness as a consequence of being lenient or tolerant
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Faintest approval here, since the mercifulness follows from being lenient or tolerant rather than from any felt impulse, so it can shade toward slackness.

entries.definition: the humane quality of understanding the suffering of others and wanting to do something about it
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise here, since the gloss makes it a humane quality, but the word tilts down toward the sufferer where *compassion* stands level.

entries.definition: an inclination to do kind or charitable acts
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and elevated, praising a settled leaning toward kind or charitable acts rather than the acts themselves, which keeps it cooler than *kindness*.

entries.definition: the trait of being willing to give your money or time
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most concrete member: praise attached to what someone is willing to hand over, money or time alike, where *benevolence* stops at the inclination.

entries.definition: the quality of being warmhearted and considerate and humane and sympathetic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The broadest praise here, gathering warmth, humanity and fellow-feeling into one standing quality rather than pinning approval to anything done, as *generosity* does.
examples: All was joy and kindness.
expressions of gratitude for the extraordinary kindness she was treated with

entries.definition: kind and considerate regard for others
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warmer than *consideration* for the same regard for others, because it credits the attention actually paid, making the kindness feel noticed and particular.

entries.definition: the quality of being cruel and causing tension or annoyance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the cruel disposition itself, but pitched at the tension and annoyance it inflicts rather than at any graver damage.

entries.definition: the quality of threatening evil
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest word here: not an unpleasant streak but a quality that holds evil over someone.

entries.definition: the quality of being deliberately mean
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Deliberateness is the whole of the charge — not a lapse or a bad mood but meanness meant, which is what condemns it.

entries.definition: malevolence by virtue of being malicious or spiteful or nasty
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Malevolence run down to nastiness — it takes in the merely nasty as readily as the truly malicious, so it can bite without carrying the threat *malice* carries.
examples: There was a streak of spite in everything she said about her neighbours.

entries.definition: the quality of being kind or helpful or generous
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and elevated, and the broadest of these — kindness, helpfulness and generosity at once, active where *benignity* is only mild.

entries.definition: the quality of being kind and gentle
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal, and the gentlest praise here: a mild kindly temper rather than the good actually done that *beneficence* credits.

entries.definition: the quality of being kind and gentle
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same kindness and gentleness as *benignity*, but with a warmth of manner that makes it feel offered rather than merely held.

entries.definition: the quality of doing what is right and avoiding what is wrong
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises goodness as conduct measured against a standard — the right done and the wrong refused, both halves — where *goodness* names a quality simply possessed.
examples: It has connected him nearer with virtue than any other feeling.

entries.definition: a woman's virtue or chastity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same weighted word as *honour* in its American spelling: a woman's chastity treated as her good name rather than as conduct.

entries.definition: a woman's virtue or chastity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Raises a woman's chastity to a matter of standing — something she is credited with and can be stripped of — where *virtue* only calls it moral; British spelling of *honor*.

entries.definition: morality with respect to sexual relations
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving but plain, naming sexual conduct as a moral good in itself without *honour*'s sense of a reputation that can be taken away.
examples: a sister's sense of decency and virtue in such a point should admit of doubt
how little of permanent happiness could belong to a couple who were only brought together because their passions were stronger than their virtue

entries.definition: the trait of being unduly vain and conceited; false pride
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The harder verdict, charging a fixed and inflated estimate of one's own merit rather than the hollow self-admiration *vanity* names.

entries.definition: the trait of being unduly vain and conceited; false pride
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The softer of the two: it convicts the self-regard of being empty, pride with nothing under it, where *conceit* convicts the judgement behind it.
examples: Vanity and pride are different things, though the words are often used synonymously.
Such as vanity and pride.

entries.definition: a ludicrous folly
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Folly pushed to the ludicrous, so it draws laughter on top of the blame that *foolishness* alone earns.
examples: the crowd laughed at the absurdity of the clown's behavior

entries.definition: the trait of acting stupidly or rashly
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weighty condemnation of the trait, treating stupid or rash action as a fault with consequences rather than a slip.
examples: her ignorance and folly had contributed to his amusement

entries.definition: the trait of acting stupidly or rashly
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain name for the same trait of acting stupidly or rashly, blunt where *folly* is grave.

entries.definition: the trait of being injudicious
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mildest here, faulting the judgement rather than the sense, and stopping well short of *folly*'s stupidity or rashness.

entries.definition: a lack of caution in practical affairs
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the fault as an absence — caution simply not brought to practical affairs — and stops short of accusing anyone of charging ahead, which *rashness* does.
examples: Elizabeth had frequently united with Jane in an endeavour to check the imprudence of Catherine and Lydia
I see the imprudence of it.

entries.definition: the trait of acting rashly and without prudence
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Heavier because it fixes the fault as a trait of the person rather than a gap in a decision: acting, and acting without prudence, not merely lacking it.

entries.definition: the quality of conforming to standards of propriety and morality
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The strongest of these because it answers to morality as well as propriety, making it a floor one can be accused of falling below.

entries.definition: propriety in manners and conduct
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Locates propriety in the visible layer — manners and conduct — commending the observance of form rather than any feeling behind it.

entries.definition: a sense of propriety and consideration for others
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Turns propriety outward, joining the sense of what is fitting to consideration for other people, where *decorum* asks only that the form be kept.
examples: a place where the company of others must be accepted with good grace

entries.definition: formality and propriety of manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same formality and propriety of manner as *reserve*, but carried as an unassuming bearing rather than as distance.

entries.definition: correct or appropriate behavior
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain name for the standard — approving only in that it marks behavior as correct or appropriate, without the warmth *grace* adds.
examples: Mr. Darcy, with grave propriety, requested to be allowed the honour of her hand, but in vain.
Miss Darcy... could not have appeared with propriety in a different manner.

entries.definition: formality and propriety of manner
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names correctness of manner as formality, so the coolness and the holding back are part of what is described rather than praise of it.

entries.definition: formal or perfunctory politeness
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The family's floor: politeness as observed form, either done correctly or gone through with no interest at all, which is why it approves far less warmly than *graciousness*.
examples: his formal civility was just what it had been
hurrying off as if eager to escape from Mrs. Bennet's civilities

entries.definition: a courteous manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The unmarked term for the manner itself, with no standard, object or degree attached; every word beside it adds one of those.

entries.definition: courteous regard for people's feelings
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same courteous regard for feelings as *respect*, but with a yielding in it — the regard shows itself by giving way.
examples: in deference to your wishes

entries.definition: courtesy towards women
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Defined by whom the courtesy is shown to — women — so it marks its object where *courtesy* marks only the manner.

entries.definition: excellence of manners or social conduct
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Not merely meeting the standard of manners but excelling at it, which puts it at the top of this family where *civility* sits at the bottom.

entries.definition: a courteous manner that respects accepted social usage
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plainest name for conduct that respects accepted usage, so mild that the approval barely registers as praise beside *politeness*.

entries.definition: courteous regard for people's feelings
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Aims the courtesy at what another person feels rather than at a code of conduct, so it credits attention where *politeness* credits only correctness.
examples: out of respect for his privacy

entries.definition: overly eager speed (and possible carelessness)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Graver and more formal than *hurry* - the over-eagerness sounds like a fault being named, with the carelessness pressing right behind it.
examples: he soon regretted his haste
He regretted his haste in accepting the first offer he was given.

entries.definition: overly eager speed (and possible carelessness)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word for speed that has got ahead of itself, and it leaves the carelessness a risk rather than a verdict.
examples: He was sorry afterwards for the hurry with which he had written the letter.

entries.definition: a rate (usually rapid) at which something happens
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The bare measure of how fast something happens, with none of the reproach that *haste* attaches to the same quickness.
examples: the project advanced with gratifying speed

entries.definition: a rate (usually rapid) at which something happens
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Names that same rate as a quality something possesses, so it carries a lift of admiration where *speed* stays a flat reading.

entries.definition: any admirable quality or attribute
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same admirable attribute framed as something to a thing's credit, weighable point by point against *fault*.
examples: work of great merit
Miss Bennet eagerly disclaimed all extraordinary merit, and threw back the praise on her sister's warm affection.
construction is not the highest merit, the choicest gift, of the novelist

entries.definition: the high value or worth of something
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts the height into the word itself - not worth but worth pitched high, where *worth* names the quality without ranking it.
examples: her price is far above rubies

entries.definition: the quality (positive or negative) that renders something desirable or valuable
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Unsigned by design: it takes the quality positive or negative alike, so it appraises where *virtue* and *fault* have already decided.
examples: the Shakespearean Shylock is of dubious value in the modern world

entries.definition: any admirable quality or attribute
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Presents an attribute as admirable in itself, already judged and approved, where *value* only weighs.

entries.definition: the quality that renders something desirable or valuable or useful
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plainly positive and broad, covering what makes a thing desirable, valuable or merely useful, with none of *price*'s insistence that the quality is great.

entries.definition: the quality of being morally wrong in principle or practice
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The absolute term of the family - it names moral wrongness itself, and covers the principle held as much as the practice done.
examples: attempts to explain the origin of evil in the world
She could not believe there was so much evil in one man.

entries.definition: the quality of being something that holds you back
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults a thing for weighing on you and hampering you, a practical drag rather than the moral verdict *evil* passes.

entries.definition: the quality of an embarrassing situation
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Locates the trouble in the embarrassment of a situation, so the discomfort is felt rather than the ranked shortfall of *inferiority*.
examples: he sensed the awkwardness of his proposal

entries.definition: a failing or deficiency
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the failing inside the thing as something missing or broken, a harder reading of the same deficiency than *shortcoming* gives.
examples: that interpretation is an unfortunate defect of our lack of information
And your defect is a propensity to hate everybody.
it is better to know as little as possible of the defects of the person with whom you are to pass your life

entries.definition: the quality of having an inferior or less favorable position
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain, unheated name for standing lower or less favourably, stating the position without accusing the thing that holds it.

entries.definition: the quality of being a hindrance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weighs the thing as a hindrance, something in the way of getting on, rather than an emptiness in it as *defect* has.

entries.definition: the quality of being a competitive disadvantage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sets the thing below its rivals as a matter of competition, judging where *disadvantage* only reports an unfavourable position.

entries.definition: the quality of being limited or restricted
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Marks a boundary — limited or restricted — with no failing charged to anyone, which keeps it flatter than *defect*.

entries.definition: the disadvantage or painful consequences of an action or condition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest here, since the disadvantage comes as painful consequence earned by an action or condition, not merely suffered.
examples: neglected his health and paid the penalty

entries.definition: a failing or deficiency
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Takes the same failing as falling short of a mark, which leaves the thing whole in a way *defect* does not.

entries.definition: a poor example
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Rueful where *excuse* is blunt - the same verdict of inadequacy, delivered with a wince rather than a sneer.
examples: it was an apology for a meal
The cold soup and dry bread were an apology for a dinner.

entries.definition: an item of information that is typical of a class or group
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain unmarked word for a typical item, carrying neither the explanatory duty of *illustration* nor the scrutiny of *specimen*.
examples: this patient provides a typical example of the syndrome
there is an example on page 10

entries.definition: an instance that does not conform to a rule or generalization
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Positional rather than evaluative - the instance is defined by not fitting the rule, and the word passes no judgement on it for that.
examples: all her children were brilliant; the only exception was her last child
an exception tests the rule

entries.definition: a poor example
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Flatly dismissive - the thing is put forward as an example and judged to fall short of being one.
examples: a poor excuse for an automobile
That leaking shed is a poor excuse for a house.

entries.definition: an item of information that is typical of a class or group
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral, and the instance is offered to make the class visible - explanatory work that *instance* makes no claim to.

entries.definition: an item of information that is typical of a class or group
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The barest of the neutral terms - one case counted off, with none of the demonstrative purpose of *illustration*.
examples: About the court, such instances of elegant breeding are not uncommon.
a wonderful instance of advice being given on such a point without being resented

entries.definition: an example that is used to justify similar occurrences at a later time
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Gives the instance forward reach - an example that licenses what comes after it rather than just typifying a group.

entries.definition: an example regarded as typical of its class
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Clinical - the instance is held up and inspected as a stand-in for its class, where *example* merely names it.

entries.definition: anything that tends to arouse
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Brisk and slightly formal, it names a thing purely by its power to rouse, carrying none of the happiness built into *delight*.
examples: his approval was an added fillip

entries.definition: something or someone that provides a source of happiness
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The fullest of these — the person or thing is named for the depth of happiness it supplies, not for being merely agreeable like *pleasure*.
examples: a joy to behold
The garden was a joy to everyone who saw it.

entries.definition: an impracticable and illusory idea
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Adds unworkability to falseness — the idea is not only illusory but could never be carried out, and the word keeps the burst inside it.
examples: he didn't want to burst the newcomer's bubble

entries.definition: something many people believe that is false
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest way to call a widely held belief false, treating the error as a passing notion rather than an indictment of anyone holding it.
examples: The notion that lightning never strikes the same place twice is an old fancy.

entries.definition: something many people believe that is false
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sharper than *fancy*: the false belief is cast as something wished into being, so holding it looks like self-indulgence rather than a slip.

entries.definition: a preset plan of action in team sports
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely technical - a single move settled in advance and belonging to the team's game, passing no verdict on whether the plan is any good.

entries.definition: a plan of action adopted by an individual or social group
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Adoption is what it adds - the plan has been taken up and stands as the settled course of whoever holds it, one person as readily as a whole social group.
examples: it was a policy of retribution

entries.definition: an elaborate and systematic plan of action
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The elaborateness is the point and also the catch: a plan worked out in enough system and detail that the working-out itself draws notice, where *system* names only the method.
examples: A scheme of which every part promises delight can never be successful
It would be such a delicious scheme, and I dare say would hardly cost anything at all.

entries.definition: a procedure or process for obtaining an objective
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flattest member, a procedure or process identified only by the objective it is meant to obtain, with none of *scheme*'s insistence on intricacy.
examples: they had to devise a system that did not depend on cooperation

entries.definition: a vague idea in which some confidence is placed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The firmest of these, treating the vague idea as accepted rather than merely entertained, so the confidence carries further than in *feeling*.
examples: it strengthened my belief in his sincerity
She had a belief that the weather would turn, though she could not have said why.

entries.definition: an impression (especially one that is artificial or contrived)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faintly disparaging: the impression treated as manufactured, something staged to be taken a certain way rather than one that simply arose.
examples: he just did it for effect
He paused for effect before he said the name.

entries.definition: a vague idea in which some confidence is placed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The softest of these, holding the vague idea as sensation and claiming no grounds for it, where *belief* claims firmness.
examples: I had a feeling that she was lying
I have a feeling that it will rain before evening.
She had a feeling the shop would be shut.

entries.definition: an impression that something might be the case
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal and unpretentious, owning the guess as a guess and claiming none of the insight *intuition* claims.

entries.definition: a vague idea in which some confidence is placed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest word here, naming the idea as something received without judging how well it stands up.
examples: his impression of her was favorable
I had an impression that the two of them had met before, though neither of them said so.

entries.definition: an impression that something might be the case
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Dignifies the guess, crediting it as a kind of knowing rather than a stab in the dark.
examples: he had an intuition that something had gone wrong

entries.definition: a vague idea in which some confidence is placed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Dresses the same vague idea as a position one would state and stand behind, more assertive than *impression* though no better founded.
examples: to adopt any opinions that came in her way

entries.definition: the impression that something is present
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral and bodily, naming not a guess about how things are but the sense that something is there.
examples: he felt the presence of an evil force

entries.definition: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The lightest and most directional of these: it points at the outcome without the justifying weight *purpose* carries.
examples: it was created with the conscious aim of answering immediate needs

entries.definition: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Makes the intended outcome sound worked out in advance, a shape already settled on rather than the bare wish *intention* names.
examples: "Is that his design in settling here?"
coming into Hertfordshire with the design of selecting a wife

entries.definition: the ultimate goal for which something is done
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Sets the outcome as the ultimate one, the point everything else is serving, and carries the figure of a journey's end that *object* does not.

entries.definition: the state of affairs that a plan is intended to achieve and that (when achieved) terminates behavior intended to achieve it
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Abstract and cool, naming the outcome as the terminus at which the behaviour stops, where *goal* names the same thing as something worked toward.

entries.definition: the state of affairs that a plan is intended to achieve and that (when achieved) terminates behavior intended to achieve it
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest everyday word for the achievement a plan runs to and stops at, warmer and less abstract than *end* for the same thing.

entries.definition: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Clipped and formal beside *intention*, stating the outcome as something fixed on rather than merely entertained.
examples: his intent was to provide a new translation

entries.definition: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the anticipated outcome in the mind of whoever is acting, so it holds whether or not anything is done about it, unlike *target* with its attainable thing to be hit.
examples: "We acted with the best intentions."
Thus much for my general intention in favour of matrimony

entries.definition: the goal intended to be attained (and which is believed to be attainable)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Dry and formal, presenting the wanted outcome as a definite thing to be got and believed gettable, without *target*'s invitation to score a hit or a miss.
examples: the sole object of her trip was to see her children
The object of the meeting was to settle the dispute.

entries.definition: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The weightiest of the plain words for a wanted outcome: it frames that outcome as what gives the planned action its reason, where *aim* only gives it a direction.
examples: my mother's purpose will be answered
She was going to the butcher's, she told me, on purpose to order in some meat on Wednesday

entries.definition: the goal intended to be attained (and which is believed to be attainable)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The sharpest of these: it makes the attainable outcome a thing to be struck, so falling short of it registers as a miss.

entries.definition: an inclination to favor one group or view or opinion over alternatives
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain name for an uneven leaning toward one side over the alternatives — it says the scales are tipped without saying the case is already closed, which is what *prejudice* adds.
examples: I do not trust my own partiality.
the strong sisterly partiality which made any admiration of Elizabeth appear perfectly natural

entries.definition: a partiality that prevents objective consideration of an issue or situation
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest word here, because the leaning has hardened into an obstruction: the issue can no longer get an objective hearing at all.

entries.definition: a partiality for some particular place
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the leaning by what it fastens on, one particular place, so the narrowness of the horizon is carried in the word rather than argued separately as it would be with *partiality*.

entries.definition: a slight but noticeable partiality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Understates by design — a lean small enough to be measured rather than denounced, yet the word still insists it can be seen.
examples: the court's tilt toward conservative rulings

entries.definition: the justification for some act or belief
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain word for the justification of an act or belief, passing no verdict on whether it succeeds and presuming no wrongdoing the way *excuse* does.

entries.definition: a defense of some offensive behavior or some failure to keep a promise etc.
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Admits the fault while covering it - what is being defended is already offensive behaviour or a promise broken, whereas *defence* presumes nothing against the act at all.
examples: His pride does not offend me so much as pride often does, because there is an excuse for it.
She was then but fifteen, which must be her excuse.

entries.definition: the justification for some act or belief
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Carries the outcome inside it - the act or belief comes out justified, where *defence* only puts the case.

entries.definition: a trivial lie
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest softening: it calls a lie by an innocent name, so the falsehood is admitted but treated as too small to bother about.
examples: Sir William, how can you tell such a story?

entries.definition: a trivial lie
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Slightly more arch than *story* - the lie sounds spun and embellished rather than merely told, which makes it faintly amusing as well as false.

entries.definition: a quick reply to a question or remark (especially a witty or critical one)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Frames the quick reply as a move made against the first, so its wit or its criticism lands as opposition rather than mere answer.

entries.definition: an impudent or insolent rejoinder
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and curt where *mouth* is broad, it clips the impudent answer down to a single flick of cheek.
examples: Don't give me any lip, just do as you were told.

entries.definition: an impudent or insolent rejoinder
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt reproof - the insolent answer reduced to sheer talk, named by the organ that produced it rather than by anything it said.

entries.definition: a quick reply to a question or remark (especially a witty or critical one)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and composed, dignifying the quick reply as a proper answer where *counter* casts it as a blow returned.
examples: it brought a sharp rejoinder from the teacher

entries.definition: a quick reply to a question or remark (especially a witty or critical one)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest of these - it marks only that something came back quickly, leaving the wit or the criticism unremarked.

entries.definition: an impudent or insolent rejoinder
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal, and it hears spirit in the impudence that *lip* hears only offence in - still a rebuke, but an amused one.
examples: don't give me any of your sass

entries.definition: an event resulting in great loss and misfortune
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Ruin on the scale of *disaster* but declared in a grander, more sonorous register.
examples: the whole city was affected by the irremediable calamity

entries.definition: an event resulting in great loss and misfortune
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same great loss as *disaster*, pitched as total and past reversing, with nothing left to salvage.

entries.definition: an event resulting in great loss and misfortune
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Lifts the scale abruptly out of bad luck into great loss, and does it more bluntly than *catastrophe*.
examples: the earthquake was a disaster

entries.definition: something that causes or entails suffering
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Covers both what inflicts the suffering and the suffering entailed, a weight borne over time where *mishap* is over in a moment.
examples: I cannot think it a hardship that more indulgence is allowed to men than to women

entries.definition: a bad experience
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and physical, casting a bad experience as a single blow taken and absorbed.

entries.definition: an instance of misfortune
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The more formal twin of *mishap*, putting the weight on the luck of the thing rather than the damage done.

entries.definition: an instance of misfortune
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Shrinks misfortune to one small instance, a thing to be shrugged off rather than suffered.

entries.definition: an unfortunate development
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The lightest way here to mark a thing having gone wrong — regret at the turn events took, with no weight of loss behind it.
examples: it's a pity he couldn't do it

entries.definition: an unfortunate development
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Meets the same unfortunate turn as *pity* with a sharper note of protest, as though the outcome were one that need not have happened.
examples: I shall tell Colonel Forster it will be quite a shame if he does not.

entries.definition: an event resulting in great loss and misfortune
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Loads the great loss with grief and waste, asking that it be mourned rather than merely counted up.

entries.definition: an absence of emotion or enthusiasm
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat, general name for the condition, taking in both the missing emotion and the missing enthusiasm, and treating the whole absence as a deficiency.

entries.definition: apathy demonstrated by an absence of emotional reactions
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The measured word for the state - it reports only that no emotional reaction came, where *stolidity* reads the same blankness as a thickness in the person.
examples: She heard the news with complete indifference, and her face never changed.

entries.definition: a feeling of lack of interest or energy
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The softest word here - the same lack of interest and energy carried as a slow, heavy-lidded mood rather than as a fault.

entries.definition: a feeling of lack of interest or energy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and weary-sounding - the flagging interest and energy are framed as something drained away, where *listlessness* simply reports them gone.

entries.definition: a feeling of lack of interest or energy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Plain and unadorned: the flat want of interest and energy named outright, without *languor*'s softness or *lassitude*'s formality.

entries.definition: apathy demonstrated by an absence of emotional reactions
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Heavier and less forgiving than *indifference*: the missing reaction is treated as dullness of feeling rather than as a stance.

entries.definition: feelings of excessive pride
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Harder-edged than *vanity* - the excess sits as a fixed overestimate of oneself, the kind that invites resentment rather than amusement.

entries.definition: the quality of being worthy of esteem or respect
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Loftiest and steadiest here - not a feeling held about oneself but a worth that earns respect from outside, so it cannot be accused of excess the way *conceit* can.
examples: it was beneath his dignity to cheat
showed his true dignity when under pressure

entries.definition: feelings of excessive pride
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Deflating - names the same excess as *conceit* but treats it as a preening softness, something faintly ridiculous rather than offensive.
examples: It is very often nothing but our own vanity that deceives us.
had been gratifying his vanity by encouraging the preference which she believed she had most incautiously shown

entries.definition: a feeling of ill will arousing active hostility
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Cooler and more measured than *gall*, yet the only one here whose ill will is already rousing itself into open hostility.

entries.definition: a feeling of deep and bitter anger and ill-will
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the same deep anger and ill will as a souring the person carries, where *resentment* keeps it pointed at whoever earned it.

entries.definition: a feeling of deep and bitter anger and ill-will
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The rawest word for that deep anger and ill will, giving it the taste of bile that *bitterness* only implies.

entries.definition: the feeling of a hostile person
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest naming of the feeling — being set against someone, without the bitter taste or the nursed grievance the others carry.
examples: he could no longer contain his hostility

entries.definition: a feeling of deep and bitter anger and ill-will
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Anger and ill will that have settled and deepened, held against someone rather than flaring at them.
examples: Nor did that day wear out her resentment.
Mr. Darcy seemed to catch her words with no less resentment than surprise.

entries.definition: feeling a need to see others suffer
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heavy word for the same hunger *spite* names, condemning it as settled ill will rather than a small grudge.

entries.definition: wishing evil to others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and grave, naming the wish for others' harm itself without the appetite to watch it land that *spite* and *malice* carry.

entries.definition: feeling a need to see others suffer
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The meanest-sized version of the appetite - the need to see suffering treated as petty and personal, where *malice* is weighed as something graver.
examples: She said it out of pure spite, hoping the words would wound him.

entries.definition: a malevolent desire for revenge
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Fastens the ill will to a grievance - the harm wanted is repayment, which gives it a reason *malignity* does not need.

entries.definition: a person who rescues you from harm or danger
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most elevated of the three and the most urgent, since the help it names is rescue from harm or danger, not the encouragement of *uncle*.

entries.definition: someone who supports or champions something
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving, but aimed at a thing supported or championed rather than at a person in trouble, so the credit is for backing and advocacy rather than for relief.

entries.definition: a source of help and advice and encouragement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm and informal, casting the helper as a standing resource of help, advice and encouragement rather than a one-off saviour like *deliverer*.
examples: he played uncle to lonely students
The old teacher was an uncle to every new student who felt lost.

entries.definition: a person who belongs to the sex that can have babies
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat classification by the sex that bears children, carrying neither the age of *girl* nor the relational claim of *woman*.

entries.definition: a youthful female person
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Marks youth and nothing else, saying nothing about who she is to anyone, unlike *woman* here.
examples: the baby was a girl
The little girl was too small to reach the door handle.
Their first child was a girl.

entries.definition: a female person who plays a significant role (wife or mistress or girlfriend) in the life of a particular man
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Fixes a person by her attachment to one man and leaves the exact tie open — wife, mistress or girlfriend all answer to it — which is the possessive edge *female* has none of.
examples: he was faithful to his woman
He would not hear a word said against his woman.
He came back from the sea to his woman and his children.

entries.definition: a sweet innocent mild-mannered person (especially a child)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Fond and protective, making sweetness and mildness the whole of the person; beside *lamb* it carries no picture, only affection.
examples: She is such a dear, and never has a hard word for anyone.

entries.definition: a person who lacks knowledge of evil
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Names the absence itself rather than cooing over the person, so the warmth of *dear* gives way to something closer to unguardedness.

entries.definition: a sweet innocent mild-mannered person (especially a child)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Tender in the same way as *dear* but with the creature behind it, so the gentleness comes with defencelessness attached.

entries.definition: a person who has never had sex
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: States a plain fact about a person's experience and attaches no fondness or reproach to it.

entries.definition: someone who admires a young woman
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the feeling entirely on one side — his admiring of her — with nothing in the word saying it is returned.

entries.definition: a beloved person; used as terms of endearment
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Tender in a way that casts the beloved as small and to be cosseted, which *sweetheart* does not do.

entries.definition: a beloved person; used as terms of endearment
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Doting and unembarrassed, the most lavish of these terms of endearment.

entries.definition: a beloved person; used as terms of endearment
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Gentle and well-mannered where *love* is bare — affection kept quiet rather than declared.
examples: Write to me very often, my dear.

entries.definition: a beloved person; used as terms of endearment
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The superlative does the work — it does not merely call the person dear but sets them above everyone else.

entries.definition: a special loved one
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warmth arrived at by comparison: this one is loved specially, which implies others ranked below.
examples: the godson, the friend, the favourite of his father!
a great favourite with her Longbourn nieces

entries.definition: a man who is the lover of a man or woman
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A bare designation of the man in the relation, carrying none of the warmth that *darling* pours out.

entries.definition: a girl or young woman with whom a man is romantically involved
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat beside the endearments: it identifies her wholly by a man's romantic involvement rather than expressing any feeling toward her.

entries.definition: a beloved person; used as terms of endearment
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Homely and sweet-tasting warmth, comfortable where *dearest* is fervent.

entries.definition: a beloved person; used as terms of endearment
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The simplest of these endearments, naming the feeling outright with nothing decorative added to it.
examples: Come here, my love, and sit by the fire.

entries.definition: a person who loves someone or is loved by someone
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Works from either side of the bond — the one who loves or the one who is loved — and states the relation rather than performing it.
examples: The acknowledged lovers talked and laughed; the unacknowledged were silent.
these violent young lovers carry everything their own way

entries.definition: a special loved one
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Fondness with a stroking, indulgent hand in it, where *favourite* under the same sense is merely preference.

entries.definition: (slang) a person's girlfriend or boyfriend
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Slang, and breezily physical: it holds a girlfriend or boyfriend at a jaunty distance from the tenderness of *sweetheart*.
examples: she was his main squeeze

entries.definition: a beloved person; used as terms of endearment
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Names the beloved by the heart itself, wholesome and unironic in a way *baby* is not.

entries.definition: a woman of refinement
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Blunt and breezy where the rest are courteous — it grants the refinement but withholds the deference.

entries.definition: a woman of refinement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The stateliest of the set — it treats refinement as her whole standing rather than a courtesy paid in passing.

entries.definition: a woman of refinement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain word for it — the refinement is granted without ceremony, where *gentlewoman* makes an occasion of it.
examples: a chauffeur opened the door of the limousine for the grand lady
She behaved like a lady at every moment of the visit.

entries.definition: a woman of refinement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Deferential — respect offered to her rather than refinement described about her, and warmer than the starched *madam*.

entries.definition: a woman of refinement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and ceremonious, the courtesy held at a polite distance where *ma'am* closes it.

entries.definition: a person who founds or establishes some institution
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and unadorned - it credits the act of starting an institution and stops there, without the honour *father* confers on the same person.

entries.definition: a person who founds or establishes some institution
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Reverent - it casts the one who established the institution as its progenitor, giving the thing founded a lineage and the founder a claim on gratitude.
examples: George Washington is the father of his country
He is honoured as the father of the modern hospital.
The fathers of the new school met to draw up its rules.

entries.definition: a friend who is frequently in the company of another
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The coolest of the words for frequent company, recording the habit and withholding any verdict on the affection behind it.

entries.definition: a close friend who accompanies their buddies in their activities
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Openly affectionate for the same close, always-along friend, where *crony* leaves the fondness unspoken.

entries.definition: a close friend who accompanies their buddies in their activities
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Measures closeness in activities shared with a whole set of buddies, so the friendship is company kept rather than confidences given as in *intimate*.

entries.definition: a person you know well and regard with affection and trust
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain, unhedged word for the bond, holding affection and trust together where *associate* names only the company kept.
examples: he was my best friend at the university
"Delighted to see their dear friend again"
"I see your design, Bingley," said his friend.

entries.definition: someone to whom private matters are confided
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Defines the friend entirely by what may be told them, making closeness a matter of trusted secrets rather than time spent together as in *companion*.

entries.definition: a person regarded very fondly
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Pure fondness raised as high as the family goes, prizing the person without saying anything about trust or shared company.
examples: the light of my life

entries.definition: informal term for a friend of the same sex
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and easy, and it specifies a friend of the same sex where *friend* leaves that unsaid.

entries.definition: a member of a learned society
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Membership as conferred standing — a learned society's name for one of its own, where *member* would only note that someone belongs.
examples: he was elected a fellow of the American Physiological Association

entries.definition: one of the persons who compose a social group (especially individuals who have joined and participate in a group organization)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat term for one of the people a group is composed of, joining and taking part included but no warmth or rank added.
examples: a member of the faculty

entries.definition: someone accepted for membership but not yet fully admitted to the group
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names a person by an admission still unfinished, accepted but held short of the settled standing *member* assumes.

entries.definition: a female person who is a fellow member of a sorority or labor union or other group
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Turns fellow membership of a sorority, a union or any other group into a family tie between women, warmer than the bare enrolment *member* records.
examples: At the meeting she thanked her union sisters for their support.

entries.definition: a woman who cohabits with an important man
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A term of position rather than accusation: it fixes a woman by the household she shares and the standing of the man in it, saying nothing about marriage being broken.

entries.definition: an adulterous woman; a woman who has an ongoing extramarital sexual relationship with a man
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The censure is inside the definition rather than added by the speaker, since the word names the relationship as adulterous and ongoing; where *concubine* marks a living arrangement, this marks a breach.
examples: He kept a mistress in town for years while his wife stayed in the country.

entries.definition: an old woman
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A diminutive fastened to any old woman at all, grandmother or not - familiar where *mother* is deferential, and it shrinks her to her age.

entries.definition: an ugly evil-looking old woman
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Repulsion with nothing added: the same ugly, evil-looking figure as *witch* but stripped of any power, so it jeers where *witch* recoils.

entries.definition: a term of address for an elderly woman
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A way of speaking to an old woman rather than a way of describing her, and it lends her the standing of kin in the act of addressing her.
examples: The soldier took the old woman's basket at the gate and said, "Let me carry this for you, Mother."

entries.definition: an ugly evil-looking old woman
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts menace behind the ugliness - she does not just look evil, she looks capable of it, which is the charge *hag* leaves off.

entries.definition: a male slave
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and legal in cast, naming the same owned condition as *slave* but of a man specifically, and at a cooler distance.

entries.definition: a person who is controlled by others and is used to perform unpleasant or dishonest tasks for someone else
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Damns the person themselves as something another has made and can direct at whatever unpleasant or dishonest work is wanted, where *tool* damns only their usefulness.
examples: He was no free man in that office, only a creature of the duke.

entries.definition: a person who is controlled by others and is used to perform unpleasant or dishonest tasks for someone else
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contemptuous with a note of ridicule — the person moves and acts, but the strings and the dishonesty behind the act belong to whoever works them.

entries.definition: a person who is owned by someone
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Drops the metaphor that *puppet* and *tool* run on and states ownership flatly, which is what makes it the heaviest word here.

entries.definition: a person who is controlled by others and is used to perform unpleasant or dishonest tasks for someone else
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The coldest of the three: the person is an implement taken up for the dirty or merely unpleasant jobs, valued for nothing but being handled.

entries.definition: anyone who does not belong in the environment in which they are found
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Hardens the same non-belonging into strangeness of kind - where *stranger* says merely unknown here, this makes the person incompatible with the surroundings.

entries.definition: anyone who does not belong in the environment in which they are found
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and unjudging - it records only that the person is not of this place, and leaves open that they might belong somewhere else just as ordinarily.
examples: After ten years in the village he was still treated as a stranger.

entries.definition: a usually secretive or illicit sexual relationship
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The blunt name for the thing, stating the secrecy or the illicitness plainly where *intimacy* muffles it.
examples: He kept the affair hidden from his wife for years.

entries.definition: a usually secretive or illicit sexual relationship
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Lends the secretive or illicit tie a romantic, faintly literary glamour that *affair* denies it.

entries.definition: a usually secretive or illicit sexual relationship
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names the same secretive or illicit tie by its closeness alone, a soft covering over what *affair* says outright.
examples: Their intimacy was discovered, and both families were disgraced.

entries.definition: the psychological state of being irritated or annoyed
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The lightest way to say it, the state at everyday strength without the weight *vexation* adds.

entries.definition: a state of irritation or annoyance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and faintly belittling — a state one is *in*, flared and conspicuous, next to the settled condition *vexation* describes.

entries.definition: a lack of patience; irritation with anything that causes delay
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the state by what it lacks, and pins the irritation to one cause — anything that makes you wait.
examples: I shall not sport with your impatience by reading what he says on that point.
Her impatience for this second letter was as well rewarded as impatience generally is.

entries.definition: the psychological state of being irritated or annoyed
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain name for the state, carrying no verdict on whether it is deserved.

entries.definition: a lack of patience; irritation with anything that causes delay
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same shortage of patience heard as agitation that will not settle under delay, where *impatience* hears a demand that things move.

entries.definition: good repute
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The good is built into the word here, so unlike *name* it needs no adjective to come out favorable.
examples: he is a man of character
where they may each have a character to preserve, they will both be more prudent

entries.definition: favorable public reputation
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Adds breadth to approval — the favor is public, where *character* keeps good standing a private matter.

entries.definition: a person's reputation
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest term for what a person is held to be, carrying no verdict of its own and taking whatever *character* or disgrace is attached to it.
examples: he wanted to protect his good name
He would do nothing that might harm his good name in the town.

entries.definition: the state of being held in high esteem and honor
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The full weight of the family: not merely being thought well of but being held in high esteem and honor.

entries.definition: the state of being held in high esteem and honor
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The formal counterpart to *reputation*, stating the same high esteem and honor in a more elevated register.

entries.definition: the reputation and popularity a person has
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Treats standing as a quantity that rises and falls, and pairs it with popularity rather than the honor *reputation* names.
examples: his stock was so high he could have been elected mayor

entries.definition: a state of dishonor
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the weight on standing forfeited rather than on anything felt, a blunter word than *shame* for the same condition.

entries.definition: state of disgrace or loss of self-respect
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Reaches both ways at once, the outward disgrace and the inward loss of self-respect, so it degrades the person and not only the position.

entries.definition: a state of dishonor
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and absolute, pitching the dishonor so low that *disgrace* sounds like an understatement.
examples: suffered the ignominy of being sent to prison

entries.definition: disgrace or shame
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the disgrace or the shame as something laid at a person's door, so blame is audible in it where *shame* only records the state.
examples: he brought reproach upon his family
His conduct brought reproach on the whole family.
She lived without reproach of any kind.

entries.definition: a state of dishonor
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain name for the condition of being dishonored, weighted no heavier than the fall itself.
examples: one mistake brought shame to all his family
Her whole family lived in shame after the trial.
